chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from Aban ibn 'Uthman, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi 'Abd Allah, who said:

I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about a man whom some of the urine of beasts touches: should he wash it or not? He said: He should wash the urine of the horse, the donkey, and the mule; but as for the sheep and everything whose meat is eaten, there is no harm in its urine.

key_terms.أَبْوَالِ: urines; the subject of the purity ruling in this narration
key_terms.الْبَغْلِ: the mule; one of the animals whose urine is to be washed
key_terms.الْبَهَائِمِ: beasts or animals; the general class being asked about
key_terms.الْحِمَارِ: the donkey; one of the animals whose urine is to be washed
key_terms.الْفَرَسِ: the horse; one of the animals whose urine is to be washed
key_terms.بَوْلَ: urine; the specific impurity or substance under discussion
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; indicating permissibility or absence of objection
key_terms.يَغْسِلُ: he washes; indicating the obligation or requirement to cleanse

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the urine of horses, donkeys, mules, and edible animals in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the urine of animals in relation to ritual purity. It distinguishes between the urine of the horse, donkey, and mule, which is to be washed, and the urine of sheep and other animals whose meat is lawful to eat, regarding which there is no harm.
